identity.title: Multilayered genetic engineering strategies for tunable gene expression in Yarrowia lipolytica: advancing high-performance cell factories for sustainable biomanufacturing.

content.abstract: Yarrowia lipolytica has become an important chassis for the biomanufacturing of high-value chemicals because of its strong lipid metabolism, abundant precursor supply, and broad carbon-source utilization. However, efficient cell factory construction requires more than simply introducing a biosynthetic pathway. Imbalanced gene expression, metabolic burden, competing metabolic fluxes, conflicts between cell growth and product formation, and insufficient genetic stability can all limit production performance. Therefore, multilevel fine-tuning of gene expression is increasingly required for the engineering of Y. lipolytica. This review summarizes the genetic engineering strategies developed to meet these demands. We first discuss episomal plasmid expression and different genomic integration approaches, with emphasis on their expression stability and applications. We then review strategies for gene expression enhancement, attenuation, and dynamic regulation, including promoter engineering, multicopy integration, CRISPR activation, weak-promoter replacement, CRISPR interference, antisense RNA, RNA interference, and metabolite- and spatiotemporal-responsive regulation. Finally, future directions are discussed, including the standardization of genetic elements, improved regulatory precision, and enhanced genetic stability of industrial strains. This review provides an overview of genetic strategies for developing efficient and robust Y. lipolytica cell factories.
